paragraphs: Rav Acha, a tanna of a baraita with Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. He taught it in Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel’s name, Jerusalem Talmud, Haro'eh. Perhaps he is the man in Midrash Hanne'elam, Zohar Vayera, at ערס״ג [locator unresolved], whose prayer ended a plague in Kefar Tarsha and who renamed it Mata Mechasya. Va'etchannan, at עתקי״ב [locator unresolved]: with Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon. Jerusalem Talmud, end of Af Al Pi: the sages allotted Marta two se'ah of wine daily, and she cursed them, “Thus may you give your daughters.” Rabbi Acha said, “We answered Amen after her.” Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok said, “May I see consolation if I did not see her gathering barley among horses’ hoofs.” Regarding Miriam, daughter of Shimon ben Guryon, whom they allotted, etc., and she cursed them, etc.: Rabbi Acha said, “We answered Amen”; Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok said, “May I see,” etc. Rav Acha wished to see Rabbi Alexandri in a dream (see Pappos).
